segments.say: Let's leave the quiet hall now, slowly, and step out into the night. The door closes softly behind you. The air is cool and fresh, and it smells a little of rain. Above you, the sky is dark and calm. And all around, if you listen carefully, the night is making its own gentle music. No stage, no choir, no audience. Just soft sounds, rising and falling.

This kind of music doesn't ask anything of you. There are no notes to follow and no moments to wait for. You don't need to understand it or remember it. You only need to let it reach you. The night has been playing like this for a very long time, long before any concert hall was built. Tonight, you can simply be its listener.

Listen. The rain has begun again, lightly, on the roof above. A soft patter, never quite the same twice. Some drops land close by, others farther away. Together they make a steady, gentle hush, like a whisper that goes on and on. There's no rhythm to count and no melody to follow. Just the rain, falling, the way it always has, kindly and without hurry.

Let your ears wander through the rain. A patter on the roof. A drip from the gutter, slow and patient. A soft rush on the leaves of a tree nearby. A puddle filling slowly, drop by drop. Each sound is small. But together they fill the night with a quiet, woven music, and you don't have to do anything at all to hear it.

show.title: Sounds of the rain
items: A soft rush on the leaves

segments.say: Notice your breath again, if you like. In for four. Out for six. Maybe the rain can be your rhythm now. Breathe in as it patters. Breathe out as it softens. You don't need to match it exactly. Just let the sound of the rain carry your breathing along, slow and easy, the way a gentle stream carries a leaf.

Picture an old tiled roof at night, shining softly in the rain. Raindrops gather on the edges of the tiles, grow heavy, and fall. Water runs gently along a small gutter. A faint light glows from a window somewhere below. Underneath this roof, it's warm and dry. And the rain keeps falling, steady and soft, like a lullaby the sky has been humming all evening.

Now, beneath the rain, you might hear the wind. It moves through the trees in long, slow waves. It rises a little, rustling the branches, then falls away again into quiet. Rising, and falling. It sounds almost like breathing. A very large, very slow breath, moving across the whole sleeping town. And you can breathe along with it, in, and out.

Listen to the trees as the wind passes through them. A soft rustle in the leaves. A gentle creak of a branch. Then stillness, for a moment, before the next breeze arrives. The trees don't hurry. They sway a little, then settle. Sway, and settle. They've been doing this through many, many nights. Let your body sway and settle with them, softly, in your mind.

Here's a gentle thought for this part of the night. You don't have to make the music. You only have to hear it. So much of the day asks us to do things, to answer, to decide. But listening asks almost nothing. You can lie completely still, and the sounds will come to you on their own, one by one, like quiet visitors.

show.text: You don't have to make the music. You only have to hear it.

segments.say: And now, far in the distance, you might hear a train. A long, low sound, softened by the miles between you. The faint rumble of wheels on the tracks, steady and calm. It's going somewhere, carrying a few sleepy travelers through the dark. But you don't need to go anywhere tonight. You can stay right here, warm and still, and simply listen as it passes.

Listen as the train moves on. Its sound grows fainter, and fainter, until you can hardly tell whether you're still hearing it, or only remembering it. Just like the last notes in the hall. And then it's gone, leaving only the rain and the wind behind it. The night closes softly around the space where the sound used to be.

Let's gather tonight's quiet music together. Rain on the roof, soft and steady. Wind in the trees, rising and falling. A train far away, fading into the dark. And underneath them all, your own slow breath, in for four, out for six. These sounds are the whole concert now. No tickets, no seats, no clapping at the end. Only listening.

You don't need to name each sound. You don't need to follow any of them for long. Let them drift in and drift out, like clouds passing across the moon. If a thought comes, let it go with the next breeze. If you notice your mind wandering, just come back, gently, to the sound of the rain. That's all. Just listening. Nothing more.

Here's one more small thought. The quiet is part of the music too. Between the drops of rain, there are tiny silences. Between the waves of wind, there are pauses. Those silences aren't empty. They give the sounds their shape, the way the hush in the hall gave the soprano's voice its shape. Rest in those small silences now. Let them hold you.

show.text: The quiet is part of the music too.

segments.say: As the rain keeps falling outside, notice how warm and safe you are. The roof is above you. The walls are around you. The night is cool and wet, but here, you're dry and comfortable. That's one of the loveliest feelings there is, listening to the rain from somewhere warm. Let your body enjoy it. Let it sink a little deeper into rest.

Stay with the night sounds as long as you like. The rain on the roof. The wind in the trees. The memory of a train, far away. In a little while, we'll travel slowly through the body, letting each part grow warm and soft. But for now, there's nowhere to be and nothing to do. Just breathe, and listen, and let the night play on.
